title: Stakeholder communication workshop
description: Explain evidence, uncertainty, and the decision needed from each audience.
prerequisites: Use-case discovery and AI delivery foundations.
objectives: Write a clear decision request supported by evidence
explanation: Start with the stakeholder decision. An executive may need to choose whether to fund a pilot; an operator needs a failure and recovery procedure; a user needs to know when an answer can be trusted. Keep the factual evidence consistent while changing the level of detail.

Separate observations, estimates, and assumptions. State dataset size, baseline, evaluation conditions, and known gaps with a result. Use examples of both success and failure. Explain what changed in the workflow and who reviews the output, rather than describing capability only through model names.

Finish a working update with the decision needed, accountable owner, and next evidence milestone. Avoid treating a pilot result as a production guarantee. Maintain an accessible limitations and incident communication plan so people know how to raise concerns after the initial presentation.

terms.definition: A condition treated as true until tested or otherwise established.
A planned point at which a specific uncertainty will be reduced.
A clear statement of the choice, owner, and supporting information.

example: A fictional pilot answered 42 of 50 questions correctly on approved documents, versus 35 for the baseline. The update names eight failures, review time, and untested languages. It requests a limited second pilot rather than claiming company-wide readiness.
mistakes: Presenting a forecast as an observed result.
Hiding failed cases behind a single percentage.
Requesting approval without stating the exact scope.
exercise: Write three 100-word updates about the same invented pilot for an executive, an operator, and an end user. Keep results identical, tailor detail, name limitations, and state a concrete decision or action.

questions.question: What should determine the detail level of a stakeholder update?
questions.answer: The audience decision and responsibilities, while preserving the same underlying evidence.
questions.distractor: Changing the facts to fit what the audience wants to hear.

questions.question: What context belongs with a pilot accuracy percentage?
questions.answer: Sample size, baseline, test conditions, and important untested or failing cases.

questions.question: A pilot tested one language. What can be claimed about other languages?
questions.answer: Their performance is unverified until evaluated appropriately.
questions.distractor: The same score applies to all languages automatically.

questions.question: How does a decision request differ from a general progress update?
questions.answer: It names the specific choice, scope, owner, evidence, and next step.
questions.distractor: It avoids stating what anyone needs to decide.

questions.question: Why include failure examples in a pilot review?
questions.answer: They help stakeholders understand limits, consequences, and remaining work.
questions.distractor: They prove all future deployments must fail.
